Apple is about to launch its major new smart home offensive. A new report published by Bloomberg today reveals that Apple has three brand-new smart home devices "ready to launch." The first two products are expected to hit the market in just a few months...

Apple three brand-new smart home products about to debut

According to the report, Apple will launch a brand-new Apple TV set-top box and an updated HomePod mini around this autumn. These products "look similar to existing versions" but will feature faster chips to support Siri AI.

The current Apple TV 4K uses the A15 Bionic chip. The current HomePod mini is equipped with the S5 chip, the same processor used in the Apple Watch Series 5.

More excitingly, Apple's highly anticipated brand-new smart home hub device is also "ready to launch." According to the report, the product is currently planned to debut between "October and early next year."

The product currently has two versions under development. One features "a screen mounted on a semicircular base," while the other is designed to be "attached to the wall via a brand-new magnetic system."

Today's report also once again mentions the device's specifications and features. According to the report, it will feature a 7-inch square display, with Siri AI at its core. It runs a "brand-new operating system" based on tvOS. The interface is described as a "fusion" of tvOS and watchOS, including apps, icons, and widgets.

It will also support FaceTime, home security monitoring, HomeKit integration, as well as customisable watch faces similar to Apple Watch.

However, the most anticipated feature is expected to be facial recognition:

Finally, Bloomberg noted that Apple has two other smart home products in development, expected to launch later. These include a "premium robotic version of the home hub" with a 9-inch display, and an "advanced indoor security camera."
